T: Put a fence in front of these men...and they'll climb it.
D: Allied prisoners in a new German camp dig three tunnels at once to break 250 men out under the guards' noses.
P: Pour the moonshine when the camp celebrates the Fourth of July.
S: Tom, Dick and Harry sausage rolls
Pork and sage sausage rolls in threes. Three tunnels dug at once: Tom, Dick and Harry.

Mix the mince, onion, carrot, breadcrumbs and sage with salt and pepper. Halve the pastry sheets, lay a log of filling along each and roll up, sealing with egg. Cut into short lengths, brush with egg and bake at 200C until puffed and golden. Serve hot with the brown sauce.
Brown lentil and onion dip with crisps, dark as tunnel dirt.

Blitz the lentils with 1 garlic clove, the spices, 2 tbsp oil, lemon juice and a splash of water until smooth. Brush the bread with the rest of the oil and toast until golden. Rub the toasts with the other cut garlic clove. Spoon the dip into a bowl, scatter with parsley and serve with the toasts.
M: Escape committee beef and barley stew
Beef and barley stew, ladled thick, enough to dig a tunnel on.

Toss the beef in seasoned flour and brown it in batches in the oil. Add the onions and carrots, then the barley, stock and bay leaves, and simmer covered until tender. Rub the butter into the self-raising flour with the parsley and salt, then stir in enough cold water for a soft dough. Drop spoonfuls onto the stew, cover and simmer until the dumplings are puffed.
Crisp potato rösti with bratwurst. Hilts rides for the Swiss fence.

Par-boil the whole potatoes for 10 minutes, cool, then grate coarsely and season. Melt half the butter in a pan, press in the potato and fry until a golden crust forms, then flip and crisp the other side with the rest of the butter. Fry the bratwurst and onion until browned. Cut the rosti into wedges and serve with the bratwurst, onion, sauerkraut and mustard.
W: Buttery jam drop biscuits, one for every bounce of the baseball off the cooler wall.

Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the egg and vanilla and mix in the flour. Roll into 24 balls, set them on lined trays, press a dip in each and fill with jam. Bake at 180C for 12 to 15 minutes until golden, then cool on the trays.
K: Clear spirit poured into tin mugs. Bartlett calls the potato moonshine shattering.
Pour 60ml vodka into each of 4 tin mugs. Top with apple juice and a squeeze of lemon.
